rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's signs are the nine clear signs enumerated at 17:101, whose identification al-Qurtubi says was treated earlier.
rows.anchor: وهي التسع الآيات المذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sultan means a clear proof; the word is used as masculine or feminine.
rows.anchor: أي بحجة واضحة بينة، وهو

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative identifies the clear authority as the Torah.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالسلطان التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These three directed hostility to Moses: Pharaoh was king, Haman minister, and Korah wealthy; Korah's unbelief matched theirs.
rows.anchor: خصهم بالذكر لأن مدار التدبير في عداوة موسى كان عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unable to answer Moses, they dismissed his miracles as sorcery.
rows.anchor: لما عجزوا عن معارضته حملوا المعجزات على السحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth Moses brought was the manifest miracle.
rows.anchor: جاءهم بالحق من عندنا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says this was renewed killing: Pharaoh had stopped killing boys after Moses's birth, then resumed it when Moses was sent.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: هذا قتل غير القتل الأول

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Pharaoh sought to punish Israel, deter people from belief, and prevent their numbers being strengthened by male children.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: هذا قتل غير القتل الأول لأن فرعون

words: وَمَا كَيْدُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says plagues—frogs, lice, blood, and flood—preoccupied Pharaoh's people until Israel left Egypt and God drowned them.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: هذا قتل غير القتل الأول لأن فرعون

words: وَمَا كَيْدُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plot ends in loss and ruin: even persecution cannot keep people from belief, so the plot comes to nothing.
rows.anchor: أي في خسران وهلاك، وإن الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqtul is jussive as the response to a command, and li-yadʿu is jussive as an imperative; dharuni is imperative in form but indeclinable, not jussive.
rows.anchor: «أقتل» جزم لأنه جواب الأمر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation supposes Pharaoh had been warned that Moses might pray against him and be answered; Pharaoh taunted them to let him pray.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذا يدل على أنه قيل لفرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the reported taunt, Pharaoh tells them not to be intimidated by Moses's Lord, claiming it has no reality and that he is their highest lord.
rows.anchor: أي لا يهولنكم ما يذكر من ربه فإنه لا حقيقة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing their religion means replacing their worship of Pharaoh with worship of Moses's Lord.
rows.anchor: أي عبادتكم لي إلى عبادة ربه

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If he cannot change their religion, Pharaoh fears Moses will cause dissension among people.
rows.anchor: أي يقع بين الناس بسببه الخلاف

rows.speaker: المدنيون وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وابن عامر وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These readers have wa-an yuzhira, with the conjunction meaning and.
rows.anchor: وقراءة المدنيين وأبي عبد الرحمن السلمي وابن عامر وأبي عمرو: «وأن يظهر

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans read aw-an yuzhira, with ya opened and al-fasadu nominative; their codices also have aw.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الكوفيين «أو أن يظهر» بفتح الياء «الفساد» بالرفع

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd favors the Kufan aw reading because it adds a letter and distinction, and aw can carry the sense of wa.
rows.anchor: وإليه يذهب أبو عبيد قال: لأن فيه زيادة حرف

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas rejects treating aw as wa: it would erase the distinction between fearing both outcomes and fearing either outcome if the first fails.
rows.anchor: النحاس: وهذا عند حذاق النحويين لا يجوز

words: أَن يُبَدِّلَ دِينَكُمْ أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas explains the alternatives as fearing a change of religion or, if that fails, the appearance of corruption.
rows.anchor: أي «إني أخاف أن يبدل دينكم» فإن أعوزه ذلك أظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses seeks God's protection after Pharaoh threatens to kill him.
rows.anchor: لما هدده فرعون بالقتل استعاذ موسى بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mutakabbir is too proud to believe in God, characterized by disbelief in the Day of Reckoning.
rows.anchor: أي متعظم عن الإيمان بالله، وصفته أنه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators identify the believer as Habib.
rows.anchor: ذكر بعض المفسرين: أن اسم هذا الرجل حبيب

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli considers Shimaʿan, with dotted shin, the strongest reported name.
rows.anchor: قال السهيلي: وهو أصح ما قيل فيه

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari's History gives his name as Khabarak.
rows.anchor: وفي تاريخ الطبري رحمه الله: اسمه خبرك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi transmits from Ibn Abbas and most scholars that his name was Hizqil.
rows.anchor: ذكره الثعلبي عن ابن عباس وأكثر العلماء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari gives Simʿan or Habib as names, and also reports Khurbil or Hizbil.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري: واسمه سمعان أو حبيب

rows.speaker: الحسن وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and others say the believer was a Copt; al-Suddi says he was Pharaoh's cousin and escaped with Moses.
rows.anchor: فقال الحسن وغيره: كان قبطيا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says he was Pharaoh's cousin and the man who escaped with Moses, explaining why he is called one of Pharaoh's people.
rows.anchor: قاله السدي. قال: وهو الذي نجا مع موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies him with the man who came running from the farthest part of the city to warn Moses at 28:20.
rows.anchor: وهذا الرجل هو المراد بقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh's household had no believer besides this man, Pharaoh's wife, and the believer who warned Moses that the council planned to kill him.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لم يكن من آل فرعون مؤمن غيره

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report calls three people ṣiddiqūn: Habib of Ya-Sin, Pharaoh's believer, and Abu Bakr, the best of them.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report consoles the Prophet: he should not be surprised by the polytheists among his own people.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا تسلية للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أي لا تعجب من مشركي قومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer's standing with Pharaoh explains why Pharaoh did not harm him.
rows.anchor: وكان هذا الرجل له وجاهة عند فرعون فلهذا لم يتعرض له بسوء

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Another report from al-Suddi makes the believer an Israelite who concealed his faith from Pharaoh's people, requiring fronted-and-delayed word order.
rows.anchor: يكتم إيمانه من آل فرعون عن السدي أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If he was Coptic, min describes his affiliation as a member or relative of Pharaoh's household; if Israelite, it attaches to yaktum as the second object.
rows.anchor: فمن جعل الرجل قبطيا ف«من» عنده متعلقة بمحذوف

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri objects to the Israelite reading: Arabic says conceal something, not conceal it from someone in this construction, and Pharaoh would not tolerate it.
rows.anchor: القشيري: ومن جعله إسرائيليا ففيه بعد لأنه يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An here means because: it is accusative after deletion of a governing preposition.
rows.anchor: أي لأن يقول ومن أجل «أن يقول ربي الله»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear signs that came with Moses are the nine signs.
rows.anchor: البينات } يعني الآيات التسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer did not doubt Moses's message or truthfulness; he spoke tactfully to restrain them from harming Moses.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن ذلك لشك منه في رسالته وصدقه، ولكن تلطفا

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh explains the dropped n in yakun as due to frequent use; al-Abbas instead treats it as the inflectional n.
rows.anchor: ولكن حذفت النون لكثرة الاستعمال على قول سيبويه

words: وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقًۭا يُصِبْكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِى يَعِدُكُمْ
rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says baʿḍ can mean all: if any threatened punishment reaches them, the full threat encompasses them; this softens admonition.
rows.anchor: ومذهب أبي عبيدة أن معنى «بعض الذي يعدكم» كل الذي يعدكم

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid's line uses baʿḍ in the sense of all, offered as evidence for Abu Ubayda's interpretation.
rows.anchor: تراك أمكنة إذا لم أرضها أو يرتبط بعض النفوس حمامها

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi says baʿḍ may stand for all as tactful, expansive speech; he cites a line about patience attaining some wishes and haste leading to error.
rows.anchor: وذكر الماوردي: أن البعض قد يستعمل في موضع الكل تلطفا في الخطاب وتوسعا في الكلام كما قال الشاعر: قد يدرك المتأني بعض حاجته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says Moses warned of several kinds of torment, each deadly, so suffering any part meant a fatal threat.
rows.anchor: وقيل أيضا: قال ذلك لأنه حذرهم أنواعا من العذاب كل نوع منها مهلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says Moses threatened worldly or afterlife punishment for disbelief, so the phrase means one of the two punishments would reach them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: وعدهم موسى بعذاب الدنيا أو بعذاب الآخرة إن كفروا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the phrase as some warning fulfilled in this world, with more punishment following in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أي يصبكم هذا العذاب الذي يقوله في الدنيا وهو بعض الوعيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view says Moses promised punishment for disbelief and reward for belief; by disbelieving, they would incur part of what he promised.
rows.anchor: وقيل: وعدهم العذاب إن كفروا والثواب إن آمنوا

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌۭ كَذَّابٌۭ
rows.speaker: المؤمن
rows.claim: If the believer speaks these words, the wasteful one is Moses's opponent to himself and a liar against his Lord.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى موسى ويكون هذا من قول المؤمن

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: Alternatively, God speaks here about Pharaoh, wasteful in obstinacy and lying in his claim.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «مسرف» في عناده «كذاب» في ادعائه إشارة إلى فرعون

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi reports that some wrongly infer a person who hides faith without verbalizing it is not a believer by conviction; he then qualifies the claim.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي: ظن بعضهم أن المكلف

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik's analogy is that a husband's inward intention to divorce his wife takes effect, just as belief and disbelief may reside in the heart.
rows.anchor: وقد قال مالك: إن الرجل إذا نوى بقلبه طلاق زوجته

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says intending disbelief makes one an unbeliever without speech, but intending faith alone never makes one a believer until it is professed.
rows.anchor: أن المكلف إذا نوى الكفر بقلبه كان كافرا وإن لم يتلفظ

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says fear or dissimulation may prevent others hearing a profession, but cannot excuse omitting it before God; public hearing protects life and property, not validity.
rows.anchor: ولا تمنعه التقية والخوف من أن يتلفظ بلسانه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: In a report in al-Bukhari and Muslim, Uqba ibn Abi Muʿayt strangled the Prophet at the Kaaba; Abu Bakr intervened and cited the verse in defense.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري ومسلم عن عروة بن الزبير قال: قلت لعبد الله

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim's Nawadir al-Usul reports Ali saying Quraysh sought to kill the Prophet three days after Abu Talib's death; Abu Bakr defended him, shouting the verse and losing a braid.
rows.anchor: خرجه الترمذي الحكيم في «نوادر الأصول» من حديث جعفر بن محمد

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says Abu Bakr's day was better than the Pharaoh believer's: the latter concealed faith, while Abu Bakr openly gave his faith, wealth, and life.
rows.anchor: فقال علي: والله ليوم أبي بكر خير من مؤمن آل فرعون إن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi limits Ali's remark to the believer's initial concealment: the Quran says he openly declared faith when Moses was threatened with death.
rows.anchor: قلت: قول علي رضي الله عنه إن ذلك رجل كتم إيمانه يريد في أول أمره

rows.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
rows.claim: Asma reports Quraysh discussed the Prophet's words about idols, seized him in the mosque, and turned on Abu Bakr when he cited the verse; they pulled out his braids.
rows.anchor: عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر رضي الله عنها قالوا لها: ما أشد شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those in the Fire dispute; the weak followed the powerful in their worldly invitation to idolatry.
rows.anchor: في النار } أي يختصمون فيها { فيقول الضعفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mughnūn means bearing a share of the weak people's punishment; naṣīb is a portion of torment.
rows.anchor: أي متحملون { عنا نصيبا من النار

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrans allow tabaʿ as singular or collective, with its singular form tābiʿ.
rows.anchor: والتبع يكون واحدا ويكون جمعا في قول البصريين واحده تابع

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans treat tabaʿ as a plural with no singular, like a verbal noun; if pluralized it would be atbāʿ.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل الكوفة: هو جمع لا واحد له كالمصدر

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash parses kull as a nominative subject.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش: «كل» مرفوع بالابتداء

rows.speaker: ابن السميقع وعيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sumayqiʿ and ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar recited kalla in the accusative.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن السميقع وعيسى بن عمر

rows.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi and al-Farraʾ allow accusative kalla as an adjective or emphasis for the pronoun in inna; Kufans call emphasis an adjective.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الكسائي والفراء «إنا كلا فيها» بالنصب على النعت والتأكيد

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh rejects this: kalla cannot be an adjective or have one, and apposition cannot replace a speaker referring to himself.
rows.anchor: ومنع ذلك سيبويه قال: لأن «كلا» لا تنعت ولا ينعت بها

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad also rejects apposition to this pronoun because it is a direct addressee, not an ambiguous referent needing replacement.
rows.anchor: وقال معناه المبرد قال: لا يجوز أن يبدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has judged among the servants; no one is punished for another's sin, and all disputants are unbelievers.
rows.anchor: حكم بين العباد } أي لا يؤاخذ أحدا بذنب غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people asking for relief are the nations of unbelievers in the Fire.
rows.anchor: الذين في النار } من الأمم الكافرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arabs use alladhūn as an inflected sound masculine plural; others retain the indeclinability of alladhī in the nominative.
rows.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول اللذون على أنه جمع مسلم معرب

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says the nūn was joined to alladhī, making it resemble the indeclinable number khamsata ʿashar.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: ضمت النون إلى الذي فأشبه خمسة عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khazana is the plural of khāzin; alternative plural forms are khuzzān and khazan.
rows.anchor: خزنة جمع خازن ويقال: خزان وخزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yukhaffif is jussive as response to the imperative; with fa it would be subjunctive, but Arabic usually omits fa in such responses.
rows.anchor: «يخفف» جواب مجزوم وإن كان بالفاء كان منصوبا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The line qifā nabki illustrates an imperative response without fa, the construction described as eloquent Arabic.
rows.anchor: كما قال: قفا نبك من ذكرى حبيب ومنزل

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Al-Qurazi says he was told the people of Hell begged its keepers for a day's relief; the keepers answered that messengers had brought proofs and told them to pray, but unbelievers' prayers are futile.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن كعب القرظي: بلغني أو ذكر لي أن أهل النار استغاثوا بالخزنة

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: A report from Abu al-Darda, cited by al-Tirmidhi and others, describes hunger, unsatisfying thorny food, choking food, boiling drink that scalds faces and cuts bowels, then the inmates' futile plea to angels.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث عن أبي الدرداء خرجه الترمذي وغيره قال: يلقى على أهل النار الجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is read with two hamzas, the second softened between hamza and alif, or with an alif between the two hamzas.
rows.anchor: «أئنكم» بهمزتين الثانية بين بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes and expresses wonder: why disbelieve in God, who created the heavens and earth?
rows.anchor: وهو استفهام معناه التوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two days were Sunday and Monday.
rows.anchor: في يومين» الأحد والاثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Andād means counterparts and partners.
rows.anchor: أندادا } أي أضدادا وشركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are the firm anchors placed above the earth.
rows.anchor: رواسي من فوقها } يعني الجبال

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb relates that the earth swayed upon water; God sent Gabriel to steady it, but winds overpowered him, so God fixed it with mountains.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب: لما خلق الله الأرض مادت على وجه الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God blessed the earth by creating its benefits; al-Suddi specifically says He caused its trees to grow.
rows.anchor: وبارك فيها } بما خلق فيها من المنافع

rows.speaker: السدي والحسن
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and al-Hasan interpret the earth's provisions as the inhabitants' sustenance and welfare.
rows.anchor: قال السدي والحسن: أرزاق أهلها ومصالحهم

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Qatada and Mujahid say God created rivers, trees, and animals in the earth on Tuesday and Wednesday.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة ومجاهد: خلق فيها أنهارها وأشجارها ودوابها

rows.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
rows.claim: Ikrima and al-Dahhak explain provisions as livelihoods and local resources, varied across towns so people depend on trade and travel.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة والضحاك: معنى «قدر فيها أقواتها» أي أرزاق أهلها

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima gives the example that in some lands people exchange gold for salt measure for measure.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: حتى إنه في بعض البلاد ليتبايعون الذهب بالملح

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak cite regional products: saburi from Sabur, tayalisa from Ray, and Yemeni ink from Yemen.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والضحاك: السابري من سابور

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The four days include the first two; the phrase means four days total, like the example of a journey taking ten days to Baghdad and fifteen overall to Kufa.
rows.anchor: في أربعة أيام } يعني في تتمة أربعة أيام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan takes sawaʾan as saying the four days were even and complete.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: المعنى في أربعة أيام مستوية تامة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ sees fronting and delay: provisions were apportioned evenly for those in need; al-Tabari chooses this reading.
rows.anchor: الفراء: في الكلام تقديم وتأخير، والمعنى: وقدر فيها أقواتها سواء للمحتاجين

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري ويعقوب الحضرمي
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri and Yaʿqub al-Hadrami read sawaʾin with genitive inflection.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن البصري ويعقوب الحضرمي «سواء للسائلين» بالجر

rows.speaker: ابن القعقاع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qaʿqaʿ reads sawaʾun in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن القعقاع «سواء» بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawaʾan may be an accusative verbal noun meaning equality, an adverbial or detached predicate; genitive modifies the days, while nominative may be a subject with lil-saʾilin as predicate.
rows.anchor: فالنصب على المصدر و«سواء» بمعنى استواء

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The phrase means provision was made for both those who ask and those who do not; God gives to both.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: معنى «سواء للسائلين» ولغير السائلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning to the sky means directing Himself to create and shape it.
rows.anchor: أي عمد إلى خلقها وقصد لتسويتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most views treat istiwa as an attribute of action, and al-Qurtubi begins to support this with a verse about forming the heavens.
rows.anchor: والاستواء من صفة الأفعال على أكثر الأقوال يدل عليه قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi cites God's forming the sky into seven heavens as support for the preceding view that istiwa is an attribute of action.
rows.anchor: ثم استوى إلى السماء فسواهن سبع سماوات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu Salih transmits from Ibn Abbas that God's command ascended to heaven; al-Hasan also held this interpretation.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس في قوله: { ثم استوى إلى السماء } يعني صعد أمره

rows.speaker: من قال إنه صفة ذاتية زائدة
rows.claim: Those who treat istiwa as an additional essential attribute say God possessed it eternally with His attributes.
rows.anchor: ومن قال: إنه صفة ذاتية زائدة قال: استوى في الأزل بصفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks the sky's transition from smoke to density; the smoke came from water's breathing, as discussed in al-Baqara from Ibn Masʿud and others.
rows.anchor: و«ثم» ترجع إلى نقل السماء من صفة الدخان إلى حالة الكثافة

words: فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلْأَرْضِ ٱئْتِيَا طَوْعًا أَوْ كَرْهًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means bring out benefits and goods placed in sky and earth for God's creatures.
rows.anchor: أي جيئا بما خلقت فيكما من المنافع والمصالح

words: فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلْأَرْضِ ٱئْتِيَا طَوْعًا أَوْ كَرْهًا
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God told the sky to bring out sun, moon, stars, winds, and clouds, and the earth to open rivers and produce trees and fruits.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قال الله تعالى للسماء: أطلعي شمسك وقمرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply omits words: they came to God's command willingly.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف أي أتينا أمرك

words: فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلْأَرْضِ ٱئْتِيَا طَوْعًا أَوْ كَرْهًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the command as subjection, like God's word to a thing He wills; on that view it preceded creation, unlike the majority's post-creation view.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى هذا الأمر التسخير أي كونا فكانتا

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi gives two views: God uttered speech to them, or a power appeared in them and served as speech to convey His intent.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى لهما وجهان: أحدهما أنه قول تكلم به

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
rows.claim: Most scholars say God created speech in sky and earth, and they spoke as He willed.
rows.anchor: وقال أكثر أهل العلم: بل خلق الله فيهما الكلام فتكلمتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says their visible compliance stood in place of speech, like a brimming basin said it was full.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنه ظهور الطاعة منهما حيث انقادا وأجابا

rows.speaker: الراجز
rows.claim: A rajaz line about a basin saying it is full shows how an object's state may speak figuratively.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول الراجز: امتلأ الحوض وقال قطني

rows.speaker: أبو نصر السكسكي
rows.claim: Al-Saksaki says the Kaaba's site spoke from the earth, and the matching spot in heaven spoke; God then placed His sacred precinct there.
rows.anchor: قال أبو نصر السكسكي: فنطق من الأرض موضع الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine plural ṭāʾiʿīn is used although the pair is heaven and earth because the wording refers also to their inhabitants.
rows.anchor: وقال: «طائعين» ولم يقل طائعتين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says their speech and response make sky and earth grammatically like rational beings.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لما وصفهن بالقول والإجابة وذلك من صفات من يعقل

rows.speaker: موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: A report from al-Thaʿlabi says Moses asked what God would do if heaven and earth disobeyed; God said a creature would swallow them, located in one of His meadows, itself within His knowledge.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث: إن موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام قال: يا رب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وعكرمة
rows.claim: These authorities read ātayā with a long alif and fatḥ; the response ātaynā means give obedience and we gave it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وعكرمة «آتيا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading meaning 'we gave obedience,' both objects are omitted; preferably it is a reciprocal verb with one object omitted.
rows.anchor: «قالتا» أعطينا «طائعين» فحذف المفعولين جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading of ātaynā means they came bringing what was within them, as explained elsewhere.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ «آتينا» فالمعنى جئنا بما فينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadāhunna means He completed and finished the seven heavens; an alternative is that He made them firm, as in the cited poetry.
rows.anchor: أي أكملهن وفرغ منهن. وقيل: أحكمهن

words: وَمِنْ ءَايَٰتِهِ ٱلَّيْلُ وَٱلنَّهَارُ وَٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night, day, sun, and moon are signs pointing to God's oneness and power.
rows.anchor: علاماته الدالة على وحدانيته وقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The celestial bodies do not deserve worship by their own virtue; God created them and could erase or extinguish them.
rows.anchor: فليس ذلك لفضيلة لهما في أنفسهما فيستحقان بها العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in khalaqahunna returns to sun, moon, night, and day.
rows.anchor: فالكناية ترجع إلى الشمس والقمر والليل والنهار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the pronoun as referring only to the sun and moon, with a dual referred to in plural form.
rows.anchor: وقيل: للشمس والقمر خاصة لأن الاثنين جمع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another alternative makes the pronoun refer to the meaning of āyāt, signs.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الضمير عائد على معنى الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine plural follows a plural of non-rational beings rather than applying masculine-feminine prevalence.
rows.anchor: وإنما أنث على جمع التكثير ولم يجر على طريق التغليب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they worship God, they should prostrate to Him alone, the one who created, formed, and subjected these signs.
rows.anchor: واسجدوا لله الذي خلقهن } وصورهن وسخرهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who arrogantly refuse to prostrate are unbelievers; those near God are angels who worship without weariness.
rows.anchor: فإن استكبروا } يعني الكفار عن السجود لله { فالذين عند ربك

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr's line about living eighty years witnesses yasʾamu meaning to tire or become weary.
rows.anchor: قال زهير: سئمت تكاليف الحياة ومن يعش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is consensus that the passage is a prostration verse, though authorities disagree about exactly where to prostrate.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية آية سجدة بلا خلاف واختلفوا في موضع السجود

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik places the prostration at 'if you worship Him,' because it is connected to the command; Ali, Ibn Masʿud, and others did likewise.
rows.anchor: فقال مالك: موضعه { إن كنتم إياه تعبدون } لأنه متصل بالأمر

rows.speaker: ابن وهب والشافعي
rows.claim: Ibn Wahb and al-Shafiʿi place the prostration at 'they do not tire,' the statement's completion and culmination of worship; Abu Hanifa agrees.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن وهب والشافعي: موضعه { وهم لا يسأمون } لأنه تمام الكلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas prostrated at yasʾamūn.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يسجد عند قوله: «يسأمون»

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says to prostrate at the latter of the two prostration verses; this is also reported from other early authorities.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: اسجدوا بالآخرة منهما

rows.speaker: أبو وائل وقتادة وبكر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Waʾil, Qatada, and Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah prostrated at yasʾamūn.
rows.anchor: وكان أبو وائل وقتادة وبكر بن عبد الله يسجدون عند قوله

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the disagreement about the prostration point is a minor matter.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: والأمر قريب

rows.speaker: ابن خويزمنداد
rows.claim: Ibn Khuwayz Mandad says the verse includes lunar and solar eclipse prayer because Arabs associated eclipses with the death of a great person, prompting the Prophet's prayer.
rows.anchor: ذكر ابن خويزمنداد: أن هذه الآية تضمنت صلاة كسوف القمر والشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi confirms eclipse prayer in al-Bukhari and Muslim; its forms vary with reports, and Sahih Muslim is the authority on the subject.
rows.anchor: قلت: صلاة الكسوف ثابتة في الصحاح البخاري ومسلم وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to every rational person; dry, barren earth is a sign that God brings the dead back to life.
rows.anchor: الدالة على أنه يحيي الموتى

rows.speaker: قوم من أهل الصفة
rows.claim: One report says the verse came when people of the Suffa wished for abundant provision.
rows.anchor: في نزولها قيل: إنها نزلت في قوم من أهل الصفة

rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: Khabbab says it was revealed about them when they saw the wealth of Banu Nadir, Qurayza, and Qaynuqa and wished to have it.
rows.anchor: وقال خباب بن الأرت: فينا نزلت نظرنا إلى أموال بني النضير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basata means to widen or spread; it may also be written with ṣād.
rows.anchor: ولو بسط } معناه وسع. وبسط الشيء نشره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghaw means they would overstep and disobey.
rows.anchor: لبغوا في الأرض } طغوا وعصوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes overreaching as seeking ever higher status, more mounts, vehicles, and clothing.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: بغيهم طلبهم منزلة بعد منزلة ودابة بعد دابة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says people given much would keep seeking more, supported by the report that Adam's son would want a third valley of gold after two.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد لو أعطاهم الكثير لطلبوا ما هو أكثر منه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says equalizing everyone's wealth would end mutual dependence and cause crafts to cease.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لو جعلناهم سواء في المال لما انقاد بعضهم لبعض

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes provision as rain: unceasing rain would distract people from prayer, so it is withheld to prompt supplication and granted so they can give thanks.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالرزق المطر الذي هو سبب الرزق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says that when crops were abundant people raided one another, so baghy here can mean raiding.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانوا إذا أخصبوا أغار بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes baghy as oppression: wealth makes people insolent and arrogant, as Qarun illustrates.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري: «لبغوا» من البغي وهو الظلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says the thing most feared for the community is the bloom and abundance of worldly life.
rows.anchor: كفى بقارون عبرة. ومنه قوله عليه السلام:

rows.speaker: شاعر من العرب
rows.claim: An Arab poet's line about early rain growing trees between two tribes illustrates how prosperity could awaken thoughts of rivalry and mutual overreaching.
rows.anchor: ولبعض العرب: وقد جعل الوسمي ينبت بيننا وبين بني دودان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Baghy may instead mean extravagance and pride, leading to dominance and corruption on earth.
rows.anchor: أو من البغي وهو البذخ والكبر أي لتكبروا في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God measures people's provisions according to what suffices them.
rows.anchor: أي ينزل أرزاقهم بقدر ما يشاء لكفايتهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says God makes whomever He wills rich and whomever He wills poor.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: «ينزل بقدر ما يشاء» يجعل من يشاء غنيا

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: God's acts always have wisdom, though He is not obliged to choose what is most beneficial; He may withhold wealth from someone whose prosperity would lead to corruption.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا: أفعال الرب سبحانه لا تخلو عن مصالح

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: Poverty is not disgrace and wealth is not virtue; God's acts remain subject to His will rather than a rule of benefit in every case.
rows.anchor: فليس ضيق الرزق هوانا ولا سعة الرزق فضيلة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas transmits a divine report: harming God's friend is war; God hastens to aid friends, and a servant approaches through obligations then extra worship until beloved, when God answers requests and supports him.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما يرويه عن ربه تبارك وتعالى قال: «من أهان لي وليا

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: In the report, God says He knows which believers are harmed by a particular worship practice, poverty, or wealth, and manages each according to their hearts.
rows.anchor: وإن من عبادي المؤمنين من يسألني الباب من العبادة

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas ends by asking God not to impoverish him, since he is among the believers only improved by wealth.
rows.anchor: ثم قال أنس: اللهم إني من عبادك المؤمنين الذين لا يصلحهم إلا الغنى
